description: Collector-grade vinyl pressing guide for Monk's Dream by Thelonious Monk – his best-selling album and Columbia debut, and the Impex Records reissue that's become the modern standard.

title: Concert by the Sea
label: Columbia
description: Collector-grade vinyl pressing guide for Concert by the Sea by Erroll Garner – recorded almost by accident for a single Armed Forces radio broadcast, and one of the best-selling jazz albums in history.

title: Empyrean Isles
label: Blue Note
description: Collector-grade vinyl pressing guide for Empyrean Isles by Herbie Hancock – the first Hancock/Carter/Williams session without Miles Davis, featuring the debut of "Cantaloupe Island," and the reissue hierarchy from original Blue Note to Music Matters.

title: Lady in Satin
label: Columbia
description: Billie Holiday's final studio album released in her lifetime, with Ray Ellis's orchestra: original 6-eye mono, a UK budget repress, and the Analogue Productions 45rpm reissue.

title: Everybody Digs Bill Evans
label: Riverside
description: Evans's second album as a leader with Sam Jones and Philly Joe Jones: original Riverside pressing, a 2024 Craft mono reissue with a disputed mastering credit, and the Analogue Productions 45rpm cut.

title: Ella Fitzgerald Sings the Cole Porter Songbook
label: Verve
description: Verve's first-ever release and the start of Fitzgerald's Songbook series: original mono set, the 2016 Analog Spark 3LP box, and an upcoming Acoustic Sounds Series reissue with a disputed mastering credit.

title: Jaco Pastorius
label: Epic
description: Jaco Pastorius's solo debut with Herbie Hancock and Wayne Shorter: original Terre Haute pressing, the Music On Vinyl reissue, and the limited Original Recordings Group 45rpm edition.

title: Charlie Parker with Strings
label: Clef
description: Parker's string-backed sessions for Norman Granz, consolidated onto one 12-inch Clef LP in 1955. This guide flags unresolved catalog-number and reissue-history conflicts rather than asserting a tier list.

title: Blues & Roots
label: Atlantic
description: Mingus's response to critics who said his music didn't swing: original Atlantic pressing, a UK London/Decca pressing, a Rhino reissue with bonus alternate takes, and the 2023 Analogue Productions 45rpm cut.

title: Portrait in Jazz
label: Riverside
description: The debut studio album of Evans's classic trio with Scott LaFaro and Paul Motian: original Riverside pressing, the Analogue Productions 45rpm cut, and the 2019 Mobile Fidelity One-Step.

title: Red Clay
label: CTI
description: Hubbard's CTI debut with Joe Henderson, Herbie Hancock, and Ron Carter: original CTI pressing, ORG Music's 33 1/3 reissue, and ORG's 45rpm audiophile edition.

title: Art Pepper Meets The Rhythm Section
label: Contemporary
description: Art Pepper's Contemporary debut, paired with Miles Davis's touring rhythm section: original mono pressing, Analogue Productions' UHQR and 45rpm reissues, and the standard OJC edition.

title: Page One
label: Blue Note
description: Joe Henderson's debut as a leader with Kenny Dorham, McCoy Tyner, Butch Warren, and Pete La Roca: original mono pressing, and two competing top-tier reissues from Analogue Productions and Music Matters.

title: Midnight Blue
label: Blue Note
description: Kenny Burrell's Blue Note masterwork with Stanley Turrentine: original mono/stereo pressings, and a genuine reviewer disagreement between the Analogue Productions 45rpm and Music Matters 33 1/3 reissues.

title: Free Jazz: A Collective Improvisation
label: Atlantic
description: Ornette Coleman's double-quartet landmark, the album that named the genre: original mono/stereo pressings, the ORG Music 45rpm reissue, and a documented pressing-defect caution on the current Speakers Corner edition.

title: Bright Size Life
label: ECM
description: Pat Metheny's debut as a leader with Jaco Pastorius and Bob Moses: original German pressing, and a documented Side A distortion defect on the 2024 Luminessence reissue that ECM has acknowledged and replaced.

title: A Night In Tunisia
label: Blue Note
description: The Lee Morgan-Wayne Shorter-Bobby Timmons-Jymie Merritt Jazz Messengers lineup's Blue Note classic: original mono pressing, the Music Matters 45rpm reissue, and a note distinguishing this from an unrelated earlier Vik-label recording of the same title.

title: Bird and Diz
label: Clef
description: The only studio recording pairing Parker, Gillespie, and Thelonious Monk, and Parker and Gillespie's last studio date together: original 10-inch Clef pressing, the Genius of Charlie Parker 12-inch reissue, and the current Verve Vital Vinyl edition.

title: Tales from the Hudson
label: Impulse!/GRP
description: Brecker's Grammy-winning fourth album as a leader with Metheny, DeJohnette, Holland, and Tyner: CD-only until 2012, when Universal Music Korea's Play 33 1/3 Series produced the first and only vinyl pressing.

title: At the Pershing: But Not for Me
label: Argo
description: Jamal's best-selling live trio date, ranked among the most influential jazz albums of the 1950s: original Argo mono pressing, and a flagged marketing-vs-matrix discrepancy on the current Analogue Productions reissue.

title: The Atomic Mr. Basie
label: Roulette
description: Basie's Grammy-winning Roulette debut with Neal Hefti's arrangements: original mono pressing. This guide flags a genuinely sprawling, unresolved reissue landscape (144+ documented versions) rather than asserting a confident tier list.

title: Sarah Vaughan with Clifford Brown
label: EmArcy
description: Vaughan's own favorite among her recordings, and her only studio collaboration with Clifford Brown: originally released simply as 'Sarah Vaughan,' original mono pressing, and the confirmed Verve Acoustic Sounds Series reissue.

title: Piano Starts Here
label: Columbia
description: A compilation of Tatum's first-ever 1933 studio recordings and a 1949 live concert, released together for the first time 16 years later. This guide flags a genuine fake-stereo concern on the original release rather than asserting a confident tier list.

title: Jazz at Massey Hall
artist: The Quintet (Dizzy Gillespie, Charlie Parker, Bud Powell, Charles Mingus, Max Roach)
label: Debut
original_cat: DLP-2 / DLP-4 (10 inch); later 12 inch consolidation
description: Often called the greatest jazz concert ever recorded, the only known quintet recording of Parker, Gillespie, Powell, Mingus, and Roach together: original Debut 10-inch pressings, the documented Mingus bass-overdub controversy, and the 2023 Craft Recordings complete box including dub-free versions.

title: Body and Soul
label: RCA Victor
description: The famous 1939 tenor sax landmark is a single 78rpm track; 'the album' is a much later RCA compilation spanning 1939-1956, and multiple different compilations share this title. This guide clarifies the distinction rather than conflating the single with the LP.

title: Birds of Fire
label: Columbia
description: The classic lineup's fusion landmark and swan song: original Columbia pressing (quality reportedly varies widely copy to copy), and a genuine trade-off between the Friday Music (Kevin Gray) and Speakers Corner reissues.

title: Ascension
label: Impulse!
description: Coltrane's watershed turn toward free jazz, recorded with an expanded 11-piece ensemble. A genuine collector puzzle: Impulse swapped takes after initial release and re-etched the dead wax rather than issue a new catalog number, creating two distinct editions under one number.

title: Study in Brown
label: EmArcy
description: The quintet's third outing, with Harold Land, George Morrow, and Richie Powell: original mono pressing, the 2007 Speakers Corner reissue, and the 2021 Verve Acoustic Sounds Series edition -- its first US vinyl appearance in some time.
